spec.population: every name the E104 face flagged as reading past +/-100%% inside an unchanged holding, deduplicated by (name, window) -- the witness list, not a screen
spec.step: a session where rep/raw moves more than 0.005; the step factor, the raw one-session read there and the repaired one-session read are published together

consistency_tests.placed_at_a_print: |raw one-session read| > 100% on the step session
consistency_tests.amplifies_the_print: |repaired read| > |raw read| on that session = the factor was applied the wrong way

spec.reciprocal_factor_read: (1+arm_read)/step - 1 = the read the same step gives with the reciprocal factor

answers.reading: 8 of 16 flagged reads are fabricated by the repair itself: the step sits on the print but multiplies instead of dividing, so the arm reads worse than the raw series

honest: descriptive census only: no gate, no verdict on the strategy, no prereg, no trial count, no ledger booking

a step is judged against the panel's own one-session reads, not against a vendor corporate-action file; a real 1:N conversion and a misprint look identical here, and the step test says nothing about which of the two a name is
plan_screen's repair semantics belong to panel_screen.neutralise; this leg publishes the defect but does not change any screened arm
reciprocal_factor_read is arithmetic on the published step, not a re-burn: the arms' other bars are untouched
